name: Making models work with partial or noisy information
gist: Papers handle incomplete multi-view data, noisy labels, and uncertain signals by using mathematical frameworks like optimal transport and information theory to extract reliable patterns.
explain: Real data is messy. Sensors fail and produce incomplete readings, labels are imperfect or crowdsourced with disagreement, images are corrupted or occluded. A reliable model should not assume perfect data. When you have multiple incomplete views of the same object — like a video frame with one camera broken, or a medical scan missing one modality — the model needs to extract the signal while working around missing or contradictory information. Information theory and optimal transport provide mathematical frameworks to reason about this.

The challenge is that standard learning assumes all data points are equally reliable. When information is noisy or partial, the model can fit the noise instead of the signal, or it might overweight the few complete examples and miss patterns in partial data. Information-theoretic approaches ask: what is the minimum amount of information needed to solve this task? Optimal transport asks: how can I match partial observations in a way that minimizes the cost of transformation? These tools help design loss functions and algorithms that degrade gracefully when data is incomplete — the model continues to learn from what is available rather than collapsing into failure because some pieces are missing.

Across 16 papers, researchers develop methods for learning from multi-view data where some views are missing, noisy labels where annotators disagree, weak supervision where labels are indirect or imperfect, and corrupted inputs. Some papers focus on reliability: training in a way that does not overfit to artifacts in the data. Others develop theoretical bounds: proving that even with 30% missing data, certain algorithms will still find the true structure with high probability. The applications include medical imaging where patients may not have all scans, sensor networks with device failures, and learning from crowd-sourced annotations.

papers.title: Adaptive Conformal Prediction via Mixture-of-Experts Gating Similarity
papers.contribution: Produces domain-aware prediction intervals that maintain target coverage while improving conditional adaptivity and tightness compared to existing conformal baselines.

papers.title: Horseshoe Splatting: Handling Structural Sparsity for Uncertainty-Aware Gaussian-Splatting Radiance Field Rendering
papers.contribution: Produces high-quality uncertainty maps while matching state-of-the-art 3DGS visual fidelity and runtime, with theoretical posterior contraction guarantees and robustness to structured covariance sparsity.

papers.title: Permutation-Consistent Variational Encoding for Incomplete Multi-View Multi-Label Classification
papers.contribution: Achieves consistent gains over state-of-the-art methods in multi-label classification with improved cross-view semantic cohesion and preservation of discriminative capacity.

papers.title: Tree-sliced Sobolev IPM
papers.contribution: Achieves same computational complexity for p>1 as TSW at p=1 while recovering TSW exactly at p=1; serves as drop-in replacement with additional flexibility.

papers.title: UniOD: A Universal Model for Outlier Detection across Diverse Domains
papers.contribution: UniOD detects outliers across 30 benchmark datasets without any further hyperparameter selection or optimization, with theoretical guarantees and superior performance over 17 baselines, providing practical convenience and accuracy improvements.

papers.title: A Federated Generalized Expectation-Maximization Algorithm for Mixture Models with an Unknown Number of Components
papers.contribution: FedGEM achieves probabilistic convergence guarantees and comparable performance to centralized EM while outperforming existing federated clustering methods.

papers.title: FedOpenMatch: Towards Semi-Supervised Federated Learning in Open-Set Environments
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on standard benchmarks across diverse data settings for open-set semi-supervised federated learning.

papers.title: GeoDM: Geometry-aware Distribution Matching for Dataset Distillation
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods with theoretical guarantee of smaller generalization error bound than Euclidean counterparts.

papers.title: Human Uncertainty-Aware Data Selection and Automatic Labeling in Visual Question Answering
papers.contribution: HaDola matches or outperforms baselines on VQAv2 and VizWiz datasets while reducing reliance on costly human uncertainty annotations.

papers.title: LANE: Label-Aware Noise Elimination for Fine-Grained Text Classification
papers.contribution: LANE achieves 2.4% average F1 improvement on manually annotated datasets and 4.5% improvement on high-noise datasets, considerably outperforming strong baselines.

papers.title: Learning a distance measure from the information-estimation geometry of data
papers.contribution: IEM is competitive with or outperforms state-of-the-art supervised image quality metrics in predicting human perceptual judgments on ImageNet.

papers.title: Learning-To-Measure: In-Context Active Feature Acquisition
papers.contribution: L2M matches or surpasses task-specific baselines on synthetic and real-world tabular benchmarks, particularly under scarce labels and high missingness.

papers.title: Reliable Neighborhood-Aware Multi-View Outlier Detection
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on six benchmark datasets by avoiding outlier propagation and aligning scales.

papers.title: Robust Multi-View Fusion via Prototype-Anchored Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.contribution: The UOT-based approach improves stability under severe missingness on multi-view action recognition benchmarks with modest overhead, with theoretical bounds on discarding arbitrary atom mass.

papers.title: Softmax is not Enough (for Adaptive Conformal Classification)
papers.contribution: Improves adaptiveness of prediction sets with notable increase in both efficiency and adaptiveness compared to baseline nonconformity scores.

papers.title: What Linear Probes Miss: Multi-View Probing for Weight-Space Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms ProbeX across ResNet, SupViT, MAE, and DINO architectures by capturing higher-order correlation patterns in weight interactions through multi-view probing.
